svg.title: Compare Producing Interests on One Capital Denominator
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-producing-interest-gross-receipt-yields; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Compare Producing Interests on One Capital Denominator; subtitle: Five illustrative gross royalty receipt yields per $100,000 invested.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Each bar measures annual gross royalty cash receipts divided by $100,000 of acquisition capital. Values are illustrative underwriting inputs, not market observations, net margins, total returns, or perpetual yields. Exclude sale proceeds, rights-trading gains, and unproved drilling upside. No payment method itself creates additional mineral yield.; caption: Compare identical capital denominators, then stress decline, commodity prices, deductions, and payment delays. These five independent examples do not sum to a portfolio forecast.; stages: label: Diversified mature oil royalties with electronic payment; value: 6% gross yield; $6,000 annual royalty receipts; numeric value: 6.0; detail: Illustrative multiwell exposure spreads single-well downtime but does not remove basin price risk. Match ACH deposits to operator remittance identifiers and production months before accepting the trailing receipt total.; label: Single-well producing NPRI with confirmed decimal; value: 8% gross yield; $8,000 annual royalty receipts; numeric value: 8.0; detail: Verify whether the NPRI is fixed or floating and whether the operator's decimal follows the instrument. One well creates concentrated downtime and depletion exposure even when recent payments appear stable.; label: Mature gas royalties exposed to regional basis; value: 10% gross yield; $10,000 annual royalty receipts; numeric value: 10.0; detail: Stress realized gas prices after regional basis differentials, gathering, processing, and other instrument-permitted deductions. A quoted benchmark price cannot substitute for the property's actual settlement economics.; label: New horizontal production with steep initial decline; value: 12% gross yield; $12,000 annual royalty receipts; numeric value: 12.0; detail: Use an explicit twelve-month decline forecast rather than multiplying a peak monthly check by twelve. Compare forecasts with completion dates, production history, and downtime to expose front-loaded receipts.; label: Concentrated legacy wells requiring statement reconciliation; value: 14% gross yield; $14,000 annual royalty receipts; numeric value: 14.0; detail: A low acquisition price can produce a high modeled receipt yield alongside severe cessation and operator risk. Paper checks and inconsistent statement formats increase reconciliation work, not intrinsic economic return.

text.title: Compare Producing Interests on One Capital Denominator
text.tspan: Compare Producing Interests on One Capital Denominator

text.title: Diversified mature oil royalties with electronic payment

rect.title: label: Diversified mature oil royalties with electronic payment; value: 6% gross yield; $6,000 annual royalty receipts; numeric value: 6.0; detail: Illustrative multiwell exposure spreads single-well downtime but does not remove basin price risk. Match ACH deposits to operator remittance identifiers and production months before accepting the trailing receipt total.

text.title: Single-well producing NPRI with confirmed decimal

rect.title: label: Single-well producing NPRI with confirmed decimal; value: 8% gross yield; $8,000 annual royalty receipts; numeric value: 8.0; detail: Verify whether the NPRI is fixed or floating and whether the operator's decimal follows the instrument. One well creates concentrated downtime and depletion exposure even when recent payments appear stable.

text.title: Mature gas royalties exposed to regional basis

rect.title: label: Mature gas royalties exposed to regional basis; value: 10% gross yield; $10,000 annual royalty receipts; numeric value: 10.0; detail: Stress realized gas prices after regional basis differentials, gathering, processing, and other instrument-permitted deductions. A quoted benchmark price cannot substitute for the property's actual settlement economics.

text.title: New horizontal production with steep initial decline

rect.title: label: New horizontal production with steep initial decline; value: 12% gross yield; $12,000 annual royalty receipts; numeric value: 12.0; detail: Use an explicit twelve-month decline forecast rather than multiplying a peak monthly check by twelve. Compare forecasts with completion dates, production history, and downtime to expose front-loaded receipts.

text.title: Concentrated legacy wells requiring statement reconciliation

rect.title: label: Concentrated legacy wells requiring statement reconciliation; value: 14% gross yield; $14,000 annual royalty receipts; numeric value: 14.0; detail: A low acquisition price can produce a high modeled receipt yield alongside severe cessation and operator risk. Paper checks and inconsistent statement formats increase reconciliation work, not intrinsic economic return.

text.title: Assumptions: Each bar measures annual gross royalty cash receipts divided by $100,000 of acquisition capital. Values are illustrative underwriting inputs, not market observations, net margins, total returns, or perpetual yields. Exclude sale proceeds, rights-trading gains, and unproved drilling upside. No payment method itself creates additional mineral yield.
